text.p: James McDougal, President Bill Clinton's former business partner in the failed Whitewater real estate deal, left for a federal prison on Sunday to begin serving a three-year sentence for fraud and conspiracy.

McDougal, who leaves behind questions about the information he has provided investigators regarding Clinton and his wife, first lady Hillary Rodham Clinton, is to report to a federal prison hospital in Lexington, Kentucky not later than noon CST Monday.
"His attitude is very good. He's telling everyone that this is just another of life's adventures and that he'll get through it," Claudia Riley, McDougal's friend and landlady said.

In the 1970s McDougal and his then-wife, Susan, along with Clinton and his wife, were investors in an Arkansas real estate venture, Whitewater, which was underwritten by a financial institution McDougal owned.
The Whitewater project and McDougal's firm, Madison Guaranty Savings and Loan, both failed, costing taxpayers an estimated $60 million.
Special Whitewater prosecutor Kenneth W. Starr is trying to determine whether deposits from Madison Guaranty were diverted to the Whitewater real estate development.

During a three-month trial last year in which both McDougals and former Arkansas Gov. Jim Guy Tucker were defendants, prosecutors said $50,000 of an illegal loan to Susan McDougal from another lending institution was used improperly to keep the Whitewater venture afloat.
The McDougals and former Arkansas Governor Jim Guy Tucker were convicted in May, 1996 following a three-month trial in Little Rock. Clinton testified for the defence on videotape.

McDougal, convicted of 19 counts of fraud and conspiracy, could have received more than 80 years in prison, but within months of the verdict he began cooperating with the prosecutors, resulting in a greatly reduced sentence.
After his sentencing McDougal backed away from his earlier insistence that the Clintons were guilty of no wrongdoing. "I wouldn't go to the bank on that," McDougal said.

In recent interviews, McDougal has hinted that Mrs. Clinton committed perjury before a Whitewater grand jury in Washington when she testified that she had done minimal work for another McDougal real estate project.
Susan McDougal has been in jail since September for refusing to answer questions from a special grand jury Starr supervises. She has yet to begin serving her 28-month term.
Tucker, who succeeded Clinton as Governor of Arkansas, resigned following his conviction for fraud.
